items.title: Cartan-Eilenberg injective resolution of a bounded-below complex
items.statement: A Cartan-Eilenberg injective resolution of a bounded-below cochain complex K is an augmented bicomplex whose terms, cycles, boundaries, and cohomology objects carry compatible injective resolutions; after translating the lower bound its indices are nonnegative and its total diagonals are finite.
items.strategy: State all augmentations, exact rows, induced cycle/boundary/cohomology resolutions, and compatibility squares. Keep the resolution data supplied and translate a lower bound b by q-b before using first-quadrant results.

items.title: Finite biproducts of injective objects are injective
items.statement: In an abelian category, every finite biproduct of injective objects is injective, including the empty and one-term cases; this assertion uses no choice principle.
items.strategy: For a monomorphism X -> Y and a map X -> direct-sum_j I_j, project to each of the finitely many coordinates, extend each coordinate map across X -> Y by injectivity, and assemble the extensions through the finite product universal property. In an abelian category the finite product is the stated biproduct; the empty case is the injective zero object.

items.title: A Cartan-Eilenberg resolution totalizes to an injective replacement
items.statement: For supplied Cartan-Eilenberg data I of bounded-below K, Tot(I) is bounded below and termwise injective, and K -> Tot(I) is a quasi-isomorphism, without Choice. Assuming DC, or supplied successive homotopy extensions for the relevant acyclic source maps, Tot(I) is also K-injective and is an injective replacement in D+.
items.strategy: Finite total degrees are finite biproducts of injectives. Filter the augmented cone in the resolved direction; exact rows and acyclic assembly make it acyclic, and bounded-below injective complexes give the derived interpretation.

items.title: Cartan-Eilenberg injective resolutions exist
items.statement: A bounded-below complex in an abelian category with enough injectives has a Cartan-Eilenberg injective resolution from supplied compatible successive choices. DC supplies the choices through three serial countable construction passes on sets of admissible finite data (in a fixed ambient universe); no proper-class simultaneous choice is asserted.
items.strategy: LANDMARK. First resolve all boundaries and cohomology, then use injective horseshoes for all cycles, then for all terms, lifting differentials compatibly. Each pass has a nonempty serial extension relation for DC; preserve the supplied-data ZF branch.

references.title: Weibel, Definition 5.7.1 and Lemma 5.7.2, printed pp.145–146; cohomology variant 5.7.9

items.title: Right hyperderived functor of a complex
items.statement: For left-exact additive F and bounded-below K with supplied Cartan-Eilenberg resolution I, define hyper-R^nF(K)=H^n(Tot(FI)), equivalently H^n(RF(K)) in D+.
items.strategy: Specify total degree and differential and tie the construction to the preceding injective replacement; independence is proved next rather than assumed.

references.title: Weibel, Definition 5.7.4 and cohomology variant 5.7.9, printed pp.147 and 149–150

items.title: Hyperderived functors are independent of the supplied resolution
items.statement: Assume Dependent Choice, or supply the required countable comparison maps and comparison homotopies. Two supplied Cartan-Eilenberg injective resolutions then yield naturally isomorphic hyperderived functors, with comparison independent up to cochain homotopy.
items.strategy: Totalize, compare both injective replacements over K, and use comparison-map existence and homotopy uniqueness. DC is used only to make the countable successive lift choices; with those maps and homotopies supplied, the argument is choice-free. Additivity preserves homotopies, so cohomology maps are natural and independent of the chosen comparisons.

items.title: Cartan–Eilenberg comparisons preserve both filtrations
items.statement: For bounded-below complexes with supplied Cartan-Eilenberg resolutions, a complex map lifts to a bicomplex map; two lifts are homotopic in the resolution direction by horizontal complex maps. Assume DC or supply the countable splittings, extensions and homotopies. Consequently the first spectral sequence is independent from E1 and the second from E2. The lifting and homotopy argument also allows an augmented source exact on terms, horizontal boundaries, cycles and cohomology, without source injectivity; the target remains injective Cartan–Eilenberg data.
items.strategy: See the completed local proof; no strategy is used as proof text.

references.title: Weibel, Exercises 5.7.2–3 and cohomology variant 5.7.9; completed comparison argument

items.title: Finite-diagonal cohomological double-complex spectral sequences
items.statement: A commuting double cochain complex supported in p>=b and q>=0 has two natural spectral sequences with vertical-first E1=H^q(C^{p,*}), horizontal-first E1=H^q(C^{*,p}), differentials of degree (r,1-r), and finite decreasing-filtration convergence to cohomology of its signed total complex.
items.strategy: See the completed local proof; no strategy is used as proof text.

references.title: Stacks Project, Lemmas 12.25.1 and 12.25.3, with explicit dual filtration conversion

items.title: First hypercohomology spectral sequence
items.statement: For bounded-below K, there is a natural first-quadrant spectral sequence E_1^{p,q}=R^qF(K^p) converging strongly to hyper-R^{p+q}F(K), after translating the lower bound.
items.strategy: Apply F to the Cartan-Eilenberg bicomplex, take vertical cohomology termwise, retain the horizontal d1, and invoke finite-diagonal first-quadrant convergence with its induced abutment filtration.

items.title: Second hypercohomology spectral sequence
items.statement: For bounded-below K, there is a natural first-quadrant spectral sequence E_2^{p,q}=R^pF(H^qK) converging strongly to hyper-R^{p+q}F(K), after translating the lower bound.
items.strategy: Take cohomology in the complex direction first; Cartan-Eilenberg compatibility gives injective resolutions of H^qK, and the other cohomology gives R^pF. Identify the total target and finite filtration.

items.title: Hypercohomology edge maps are canonical
items.statement: The edge maps of the two hypercohomology spectral sequences agree with the canonical maps induced by the Cartan-Eilenberg augmentation wherever the extremal edge terms are defined.
items.strategy: Represent each edge by inclusion or projection of the extremal filtration piece, trace it through K -> Tot(I), and compare with the canonical derived-functor map, stating each bounded edge position.

items.title: G-acyclic object for a left-exact functor
items.statement: For abelian categories B and C, an additive left-exact G:B->C, and a named supplied injective datum I at X, the object X is G-acyclic relative to I when R_I^pG(X)=0 for every p>0; a complex is termwise G-acyclic relative to specified data if every term is.
items.strategy: Define this through existing right derived objects and distinguish an acyclic object from an acyclic complex.

items.title: Applying F gives a termwise G-acyclic complex
items.statement: If F sends injectives to G-acyclics, applying F to an injective resolution I of A gives a bounded-below termwise G-acyclic complex F(I); it need not resolve F(A), and its cohomology is R^qF(A).
items.strategy: Apply the hypothesis termwise and identify cohomology by the definition of R^qF. Explicitly reject the stronger resolution claim because left exactness alone does not preserve positive exactness.

items.title: The total Cartan-Eilenberg complex computes the derived composite
items.statement: For left-exact F and G with enough injectives, if F sends injectives to G-acyclics, the total complex built from supplied resolutions computes the relative object R_I(GF)(A); the subscript may be suppressed only under Dependent Choice or supplied change-of-resolution comparisons.
items.strategy: Use termwise G-acyclicity and the right acyclic-resolution theorem to compare the total complex with a genuine injective model for the composite; DC is used only for the theorem's countable successive comparison choices, and supplied comparisons preserve the ZF branch. Verify the augmentation and quasi-isomorphism without calling F(I) a resolution of F(A).

items.title: The two filtrations identify E2 and the composite edge
items.statement: One filtration of the composite double complex computes R(GF)(A), while the other has E_2^{p,q}=R^pG(R^qF(A)); extremal filtration maps are the canonical derived-composite edge maps.
items.strategy: Compute both filtrations: one by the G-acyclic total comparison, the other by first identifying R^qF(A) and then R^pG. Trace edge representatives through the augmentation.

items.title: Grothendieck spectral sequence
items.statement: For left-exact additive F:A->B and G:B->C between abelian categories with enough injectives, if F sends injectives to G-acyclics, supplied resolution and comparison data yield in ZF a natural first-quadrant spectral sequence E_2^{p,q}=R^pG(R^qF(A)) strongly converging to R^{p+q}(GF)(A); alternatively Dependent Choice supplies the required countable successive choices for one input.
items.strategy: LANDMARK. Build the Cartan-Eilenberg double complex, identify E2 and target by its two filtrations, and invoke finite-diagonal convergence. Supplied successor and comparison data give the ZF branch; DC is used exactly to select one countable chain of compatible stages, never to make a global simultaneous selection.

items.title: Naturality of the Grothendieck spectral sequence
items.statement: Assume Dependent Choice, or supply the requisite comparison maps and homotopies. Morphisms of inputs and compatible natural transformations induce morphisms of Grothendieck spectral sequences from E2 onward, agreeing with derived maps on E2 and the filtered abutment and independent of comparison choices.
items.strategy: Lift maps to resolutions and Cartan-Eilenberg data, totalize, use filtered-complex functoriality, and apply homotopy uniqueness to prove independence from E2 onward. DC is used only for the countable successive comparison lifts; supplied maps and homotopies give the corresponding ZF branch.

items.title: Five-term exact sequence of the Grothendieck spectral sequence
items.statement: There is a natural exact sequence 0 -> R^1G(F(A)) -> R^1(GF)(A) -> G(R^1F(A)) -> R^2G(F(A)) -> R^2(GF)(A), with the fourth arrow d2.
items.strategy: Substitute the Grothendieck E2 terms and composite abutment into the library's cohomological five-term theorem; identify R^0 with the original functor and trace naturality.

references.title: Weibel, Theorem 5.8.3, low-degree sequence, printed p.151

items.title: Grothendieck collapse when one functor is exact
items.statement: If F is exact, R^n(GF)(A)=R^nG(F(A)); if G is exact, R^n(GF)(A)=G(R^nF(A)), naturally, because only one E2 row or column survives.
items.strategy: Use positive derived-functor vanishing for the exact functor, eliminate all off-axis terms, and identify the target through its one-piece filtration.

items.title: Derived composition isomorphisms under total acyclicity
items.statement: If R^qF(A)=0 for q>0 then R^n(GF)(A)=R^nG(F(A)); if every R^qF(A) is G-acyclic then R^n(GF)(A)=G(R^nF(A)), naturally.
items.strategy: Apply the one-row or one-column argument directly to E2, checking every off-axis term and then the single associated-graded quotient of the target filtration.

items.title: Dual left-derived Grothendieck spectral sequence
items.statement: Dually, additive right-exact functors between abelian categories with enough projectives and the projective-to-acyclic hypothesis give L_pG(L_qF(A)) converging to L_{p+q}(GF)(A), under Dependent Choice or with a supplied projective resolution, projective Cartan-Eilenberg resolution, and filtration-compatible comparison maps and homotopies.
items.strategy: Record all dual hypotheses and homological indexing. DC is used only for the countable successive comparison choices in the cited acyclic-resolution theorem; supplied comparison data preserve the ZF branch. Do not reuse injective data or infer projective-resolution existence without its own assumptions.

items.title: Universal coefficient spectral sequence
items.statement: For a bounded-below chain complex C of projective left R-modules, a left R-module M, and a supplied projective Cartan-Eilenberg grid with named homology resolutions P_q, E_2^{p,q}=Ext_{P_q}^p(H_qC,M) converges to H^{p+q}(Hom_R(C,M)); the resolution subscripts may be suppressed only under DC or supplied change-of-resolution comparisons.
items.strategy: Apply Hom(-,M) to projective Cartan-Eilenberg data. One filtration recovers Hom(C,M) by termwise projectivity; the other gives Ext of homology. Verify the library's chain-to-cochain convention and finite diagonals.

items.title: Kunneth Tor spectral sequence
items.statement: For bounded-below complexes C of right R-modules and D of left R-modules, with one degreewise flat and supplied projective Cartan-Eilenberg grids whose term, cycle, boundary, and homology columns are projective resolutions and whose horizontal structure sequences split degreewise, E^2_{p,q}=direct-sum_{i+j=q} Tor_p^R(H_iC,H_jD) converges to H_{p+q}(Tot(C tensor_R D)).
items.strategy: Resolve one direction by a projective Cartan-Eilenberg bicomplex and tensor with the flat complex. Acyclic assembly identifies the target filtration; the other filtration gives the displayed internally graded Tor page.

items.title: PID Kunneth is a two-column collapse
items.statement: Assume Choice. Over a PID, the free bounded-below case has only Tor columns p=0,1 and yields the published natural Kunneth short exact sequence; its splitting is not natural.
items.strategy: Use freeness of submodules of free modules to get projective dimension at most one, identify the two total-degree filtration quotients with the published sequence, and separate the Choice-dependent splitting.

items.title: UCT and Kunneth collapse retains an extension problem
items.statement: Two-column collapse determines a natural short exact sequence of filtration quotients, not a canonical direct-sum abutment. Under the Axiom of Choice, the cited PID UCT for a free complex and Kunneth theorem for two bounded-below free complexes supply splittings, but those splittings may be nonnatural.
items.strategy: Write the two-step filtration and its associated graded pieces and apply the choice-free general collapse-without-splitting result. For the separate PID comparison, invoke Choice exactly where the published UCT proof chooses free-submodule splittings; do not transfer that assumption to the generic filtration claim.

items.title: Hyper-Tor spectral sequence
items.statement: For a right R-module M and bounded-below complex K of left R-modules, supplied projective Cartan-Eilenberg data give E^2_{p,q}=Tor_p^R(M,H_qK) converging to H_{p+q}(M tensor_R^L K).
items.strategy: Apply M tensor_R - to the Cartan-Eilenberg resolution, compute Tor of homology in one filtration and the derived tensor total in the other, then verify finite-diagonal convergence.

items.title: Hyper-Ext spectral sequence
items.statement: For left R-modules, a bounded-above cochain complex K and a module M admit, relative to supplied bounded replacement data, a natural strongly convergent spectral sequence E_2^{p,q}=Ext_R^p(H^{-q}(K),M) => Ext_R^{p+q}(K,M). Dually, for a module M and bounded-below K there is E_2^{p,q}=Ext_R^p(M,H^q(K)) => Ext_R^{p+q}(M,K). Each becomes first-quadrant after translating the relevant finite bound.
items.strategy: For the contravariant branch use the finite-diagonal double complex Hom_R(K,I_M), where I_M is an injective resolution, and reverse the K-index; for the covariant branch apply Hom_R(M,-) to bounded-below injective replacement data for K. Compute the two filtrations, identify the total cohomology through derived Hom, and check the translated support and total degree before invoking first-quadrant convergence.

references.title: Stacks Project, Tag 07AA (bounded-above first-variable Ext spectral sequence)
Stacks Project, Tag 0AVG (bounded-below second-variable Ext spectral sequence)

items.title: Invariants for a group extension compose
items.statement: For 1->N->G->Q->1 and a G-module M, M^N has the induced Q-action and (M^N)^Q=M^G naturally.
items.strategy: Normality makes M^N G-stable and N acts trivially, so the action factors through Q. Check that Q-fixed N-invariants are exactly G-fixed elements and verify naturality.

items.title: N-invariants send injective G-modules to Q-acyclics
items.statement: For a group extension, (-)^N sends injective G-modules to injective Q-modules choice-free. Under DC their positive Q-cohomology vanishes; relative to a named supplied resolution datum J, the same vanishing follows choice-free when a cochain-homotopy equivalence from J to the deleted trivial resolution is supplied.
items.strategy: Inflation Q-Mod->G-Mod is exact and left adjoint to N-invariants. Inflate a Q-monomorphism, extend maps into the injective G-module, and transpose back, all choice-free for the single map. Use DC only through the published positive-derived-vanishing and resolution-independent group-cohomology interfaces.

items.title: Restriction of injective group modules is injective
items.statement: For H<=G, induction Z[G] tensor over Z[H] - preserves monomorphisms without a choice of all coset representatives. Consequently restriction of an injective G-module is injective over H; a supplied G-injective resolution restricts to an H-injective resolution.
items.strategy: See the completed local proof; no strategy is used as proof text.

references.title: Weibel, Sections 6.3 and 6.8; finite-support choice-free induction argument supplied here

items.title: Lyndon-Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence
items.statement: Assume Dependent Choice. For 1->N->G->Q->1 and a G-module M with supplied resolution data, E_2^{p,q}=H^p(Q,H^q(N,M)) converges strongly to H^{p+q}(G,M), naturally; with all comparison data supplied, the corresponding relative H_I statement remains valid in ZF. Naturality includes extension maps (N,G,Q)->(Nprime,Gprime,Qprime) and coefficient maps Res(Mprime)->M, via exact pullback-resolution comparison into injective targets.
items.strategy: LANDMARK. Apply Grothendieck to N-invariants followed by Q-invariants, use their composition and the injective-to-Q-acyclic lemma, then identify E2 and target by the existing derived-functor definition of group cohomology. DC is used exactly by that published resolution-independent H interface; the relative supplied-data construction is retained separately.

items.title: Five-term exact sequence from LHS
items.statement: LHS gives 0 -> H^1(Q,M^N) -> H^1(G,M) -> H^1(N,M)^Q -> H^2(Q,M^N) -> H^2(G,M), with the fourth arrow the transgression.
items.strategy: Substitute the LHS E2 terms into the cohomological five-term sequence and identify H^0 with invariants. Define the first edge map as inflation, the second as restriction, and the d2 map out of H^1(N,M)^Q as transgression; verify these descriptions directly on the composite-invariants construction. This is self-contained and does not import the later low-degree group-cohomology page.

items.title: LHS collapse for a cohomologically trivial normal subgroup
items.statement: If H^q(N,M)=0 for q>0, LHS has one row and gives natural isomorphisms H^n(G,M)=H^n(Q,M^N).
items.strategy: Remove the vanishing rows, observe every differential vanishes, and identify the one quotient in each target filtration; naturality comes from LHS naturality.

items.title: Spectral-sequence computation record
items.statement: A complete computation record specifies conventions, the known page, every possible later differential and its value or vanishing reason, stabilization, convergence hypotheses, the abutment filtration, extension problems, and either canonical edge maps under their stated hypotheses or directly constructed application boundary maps.
items.strategy: Define a checklist separating page computation, later differentials, convergence, and reconstruction; require structural-zero evidence and label all noncanonical splittings.

items.title: An E2 page alone does not determine the abutment
items.statement: Finite first-quadrant spectral sequences can have isomorphic E2 pages but different later differentials, E-infinity pages, and abutments.
items.strategy: Construct two bounded filtered complexes with identical E2 bigraded groups, one with a nonzero filtration-drop-two differential and one with zero; compute d2, E3, and both finite filtered cohomology targets directly.

items.title: Collapsed vector-space spectral sequences split noncanonically
items.statement: Assume Choice. A collapsed first-quadrant spectral sequence of k-vector spaces with finite abutment filtrations yields noncanonical direct-sum decompositions by its E-infinity terms, but no natural splitting.
items.strategy: Use Choice to make graded vector spaces projective, split each finite filtration short exact sequence, and induct. Show complements vary under automorphisms; retain the finite-dimensional finite-choice branch separately.

items.title: Grothendieck needs only left exactness
items.statement: False: the theorem also needs resolution existence and an acyclicity hypothesis such as F sending injectives to G-acyclics.
items.strategy: Locate the exact use of termwise G-acyclicity in identifying the total complex with R(GF); without it the advertised abutment is not justified.

items.title: R^pG(R^qF) is the E1 page
items.statement: False: R^pG(R^qF(A)) is the standard E2 page; E1 retains one unresolved differential direction.
items.strategy: Write the page after cohomology in one direction and show that taking its next cohomology produces the iterated derived functors.

items.title: Cartan-Eilenberg only resolves terms
items.statement: False: compatible resolutions of cycles, boundaries, and cohomology are essential, especially for the second hypercohomology spectral sequence.
items.strategy: Point to the definition's compatibility clauses and the use of the H^qK resolution in identifying the E2 page; unrelated termwise resolutions do not suffice.

items.title: UCT collapse gives a natural splitting
items.statement: False: collapse gives a natural short exact sequence; an available direct-sum splitting is additional and generally nonnatural.
items.strategy: Use the two-step filtration and general nonsplitting example, then compare with the PID UCT theorem's explicit separation of natural exactness and nonnatural splitting.

items.title: LHS defines low-degree group cohomology
items.statement: False: group cohomology is already the derived functor of invariants; LHS computes and relates those groups via a composite of invariants.
items.strategy: Trace the construction from H^n(G,-)=R^n(-)^G and (-)^G=(-)^Q o (-)^N; the spectral sequence consumes rather than defines these groups.

items.title: Writing E2 implies H proves convergence
items.statement: False: convergence also requires filtration hypotheses, stabilization, identification of E-infinity with associated graded target, and reconstruction extension analysis.
items.strategy: Apply the computation-record checklist, cite finite first-quadrant convergence for the actual filtration, and cite the extension proposition for what a double arrow suppresses.

title: Grothendieck Spectral Sequences and Computations — Examples

items.title: A two-row hypercohomology spectral sequence
items.statement: If H^qK vanishes except for q=0,1, the second hypercohomology spectral sequence has those two rows; d2 is the first possible cross-row differential and the target has a two-step filtration.
items.strategy: Display both E2 rows, list all possible d2 maps, eliminate d_r for r>=3 by bidegree, and record E-infinity quotients and unresolved extensions.

items.title: Grothendieck with an exact outer functor
items.statement: If G is exact, only E_2^{0,q}=G(R^qF(A)) survives and R^n(GF)(A)=G(R^nF(A)) naturally.
items.strategy: Use positive derived vanishing for G, mark zero columns, verify E2 collapse, identify the one-piece filtration, and note that every F(I) is then G-acyclic.

items.title: Five-term sequence of a composite functor
items.statement: For invariants in a fixed group extension, the Grothendieck five-term sequence specializes to inflation, restriction, and transgression.
items.strategy: Substitute M^N, H^1(N,M), and H^p(Q,-), label both edge maps and d2, and compare term-by-term with the published group-cohomology five-term sequence.

items.title: UCT as a two-column spectral sequence over the integers
items.statement: Assume Choice. For free C, the integer UCT has only p=0,1 and yields 0 -> Ext_Z^1(H_{n-1}C,M) -> H^nHom(C,M) -> Hom_Z(H_nC,M) -> 0.
items.strategy: Use global dimension one, identify the two total-degree positions under the library Hom convention, match the filtration order and edge map with the published UCT, and mark splitting nonnatural.

items.title: Kunneth as a two-column spectral sequence over a PID
items.statement: Assume Choice. For the bounded-below free PID case, only Tor columns p=0,1 survive and give the natural tensor/Tor short exact sequence.
items.strategy: Write both columns with internal-degree sums, rule out every differential, identify the filtration quotients with the published Kunneth theorem, and label splitting choice-dependent and nonnatural.

items.title: LHS for a split group extension
items.statement: For G=N semidirect Q, display E_2^{p,q}=H^p(Q,H^q(N,M)) and the section-induced low-degree behavior; splitting the group extension alone does not force spectral-sequence collapse.
items.strategy: Use the section to identify the semidirect action and split valid edge maps, compute the five-term portion, and retain every possible higher differential absent extra vanishing.

items.title: A collapse with a noncanonical extension choice
items.statement: Collapsed Z/2 graded pieces may reconstruct Z/4 over Z; over a field Choice supplies complements, but they are not natural.
items.strategy: Construct the two-step filtration 0 < 2Z/4Z < Z/4Z directly and verify that both graded pieces are Z/2 while the middle group is not their direct sum. Then contrast a two-step vector-space filtration whose Choice-supplied complements are moved by automorphisms, separating existence, uniqueness, and naturality.

items.title: Identical E2 pages with different later differentials
items.statement: Two finite first-quadrant filtered cochain complexes have isomorphic E2 pages but different d2 maps, E3 pages, and filtered abutments.
items.strategy: Put generators in source and target bidegrees of d2; set the filtration-drop-two differential to an isomorphism in one complex and zero in the other, with identical d0,d1. Compute filtered Z^r/B^r through E3 and total cohomology directly.

items.title: A complete spectral-sequence computation record
items.statement: Give the integer UCT example with convention, E2, all differential vanishings, E-infinity, convergence, filtration, extension, edge maps, and nonnatural splitting status recorded.
items.strategy: Fill every computation-record field using global dimension one for zeroes, first-quadrant convergence for the filtration, and the published UCT for edge and extension identification; never replace reconstruction by the word collapse.
